items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: So I proceeded to show Ben how to play the saxophone that way, and he always give me credit, said Budd Johnson taught me how to play the saxophone

ctx.x:
the wintertime.
So when we arrived in Amarillo, Texas it was 15 below zero! Can you imagine that? Up in the Panhandle. 15 below zero! And so when we got there Eugene Coy was really in his hometown, so he took as many people as he could to his parent's home, and the rest of us he put us up in a little hotel over a drugstore there. It was like what you may call like a shopping center, was about like a square block. They had a theater, and a hotel, a laundry, and whatnot.

So we got up into these rooms, and we slept overnight, and we woke up, and there was another musician living there at that time, and his name was Ben Webster. And this was my first meeting of Ben Webster. This was in the year of 1928. So naturally, you know, musicians used to look each other up, man, what do you do? What do you play? What are you doing? And oh --
